content: Mucopurulent discharge refers to the release or secretion of a fluid that contains both mucus and pus. The term mucopertains to mucus, while purulent pertains to pus. This type of discharge can originate from various parts of the body, including the eyes, nose, cervix, vagina, or other areas, and is typically associated with infection and inflammation. In ophthalmology, mucopurulent discharge from the eyes, which may become encrusted on the eyelashes, is a characteristic sign of bacterial conjunctivitis. It is important to distinguish this from the normal accumulation of tears, mucus, and debris (commonly referred to as rheum) that can collect at the edges of the eyelids after sleep. Unlike mucopurulent discharge, this normal buildup does not contain pus. In obstetrics and gynecology, mucopurulent discharge from the cervix or vagina can be indicative of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). PID is often associated with infections caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Chlamydia trachomatis. Women with PID typically present with additional symptoms, including lower abdominal tenderness, bilateral adnexal tenderness, and cervical motion tenderness.
